overallSummary: Fabio Giglietto maintains a strong, highly targeted academic and professional social media presence across Bluesky, Mastodon, and LinkedIn, with a total following of 3,580. His content is highly specialized, focusing on computational social science, disinformation, and coordinated inauthentic behavior. Across all platforms, he achieves exceptional engagement rates, driven by a community of peers, students, and researchers interested in his team's methodology, tool releases (like CooRnet), and academic opportunities.

contentThemes.description: Updates on research publications, methodology discussions, and conference presentations regarding coordinated social media campaigns.
Announcements of new software versions and algorithmic improvements, specifically regarding the CooRnet tool.
Promotion of postdoctoral fellowships, PhD opportunities, and research grant milestones within his lab.

recommendations: Leverage Bluesky's highly active academic community for recruiting by cross-posting detailed application links directly when announcing opportunities.
Increase visual engagement on LinkedIn by adding images, slide decks, or infosec diagrams when announcing major milestones like new grants or research papers.
Utilize Mastodon threads to host deeper, technical Q&A sessions on the methodologies behind CooRnet updates to engage the platform's developer-heavy audience.

platformInsights.bluesky: Bluesky delivers the highest engagement rate (average ~6.14% per post), driven by robust sharing/reposting behavior around academic opportunities and newly published research.
platformInsights.mastodon: Mastodon provides a highly focused niche audience. While follower counts are lower, technical updates like CooRnet v2.0 generate high relative engagement and quality peer interactions.
platformInsights.linkedin: LinkedIn acts as the primary driver for broad professional reach and visibility. It excels for high-impact professional milestones, yielding the highest absolute volume of likes and comments.

topPerformingContent.content: Just published our new paper on coordinated inauthentic behavior on social media platforms!
New research opportunity for PhD students interested in computational social science. Reply for details!
Excited to announce that our research team has been awarded a new grant to study information operations across social media platforms.
Our team has just released v2.0 of CooRnet, with improved algorithms for detecting coordinated link sharing behavior.
